children: The benchmark indices closed nearly 1 percent higher despite some profit-booking at elevated levels, supported by positive market breadth. Around 2,319 stocks advanced, while 1,021 declined on the NSE. The market may attempt to sustain its upward momentum in the coming sessions, although intermittent bouts of profit-booking and consolidation cannot be ruled out. Here are some short-term trading ideas for investors and traders to consider:
Himanshu Gupta, Associate Vice President - Research-Technical Department at Jainam
Devyani International | CMP: Rs 132.03

Devyani International has broken out of its falling channel, surging 4.26 percent to close at Rs 132.03, near its day's high of Rs 133.44, on strong volumes of 2.82 million shares. After a sharp correction from its high of Rs 155.95, the stock found support in the Rs 113–115 zone and has since moved above the upper trendline of the descending channel.

The stock has also reclaimed its 20-day EMA (Rs 124.59) and 50-day EMA (Rs 126.54), indicating a revival in short-term momentum. It is currently trading around the Rs 132–133 resistance zone. A decisive close above this level would confirm the breakout and open the door for further upside towards Rs 145, its previous swing high.
The RSI at 61.79 is moving higher, signalling improving strength and indicating room for further upside. The technical structure remains positive as long as the stock holds above the Rs 124–125 zone.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 145
Stop-Loss: Rs 124
Fertilizers and Chemicals Travancore | CMP: Rs 813.25

FACT has registered a strong breakout from its falling channel, surging 8.67 percent to close at Rs 813.25, against its day's high of Rs 835, on heavy volumes of 4.06 million shares. After a prolonged correction from its high of Rs 1,058, the stock found support near the Rs 659 zone. It has now cleared the upper trendline of the channel and closed above the Rs 803–804 resistance zone.

The stock is trading comfortably above its 20-day EMA (Rs 736) and 50-day EMA (Rs 752), indicating a strong revival in momentum. Sustaining above Rs 803 would confirm the breakout and open the door for further upside towards Rs 880–920, its previous swing-high zone.

The RSI at 68.57 reflects strong momentum, although the Stochastic RSI at 91.6 is in the overbought zone. Therefore, some minor consolidation or profit-booking cannot be ruled out in the near term. The technical structure remains positive as long as the stock holds above the Rs 770–780 zone.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 880
Stop-Loss: Rs 770
Sky Gold and Diamonds | CMP: Rs 983.4

Sky Gold and Diamonds has extended its recovery, gaining 4.55 percent to close at Rs 983.40, near its day's high of Rs 991.85, on volumes of 1.27 million shares. After a sharp correction from its high of Rs 1,084, the stock found support near the Rs 763 zone and has since formed a base above its 50-day EMA (Rs 879) and rising trendline.

The stock is trading above its 20-day EMA (Rs 933) and is now testing the downward-sloping trendline, along with the resistance zone around Rs 993. A decisive close above Rs 995 would confirm the breakout and open the door for further upside towards Rs 1,040–1,080.
The RSI at 59.89 is moving higher, signalling improving strength and indicating room for further upside. The technical structure remains positive as long as the stock holds above the Rs 925–930 zone.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 1,040
Stop-Loss: Rs 925
Sudeep Shah, Head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities
Federal Bank | CMP: Rs 361.6

Federal Bank has broken out above a downward-sloping trendline on the daily chart, indicating the continuation of its broader uptrend. The RSI has moved up sharply, signalling improving momentum and renewed buying interest.

Additionally, the stock has closed above the upper Bollinger Band, a development often associated with the beginning of a strong trending phase. Its ability to hold above the 20-week EMA last week further reinforces the underlying strength.

Going ahead, the bullish bias is likely to remain intact, with the breakout gaining further credibility if the stock sustains above the breakout zone. Hence, accumulation is recommended in the Rs 359–364 zone, with a stop-loss at Rs 352. On the upside, the stock is likely to test Rs 385 in the short term.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 385
Stop-Loss: Rs 352
Canara Bank | CMP: Rs 132.3

Canara Bank has broken out above a downward-sloping trendline on the daily chart, backed by a strong surge in volumes, lending credibility to the breakout. The stock is now trading above its key short-term and long-term moving averages, reflecting a significant improvement in its price structure.

The RSI has also broken above a horizontal resistance trendline, signalling a renewed pickup in bullish momentum. Adding to the positive outlook, the PSU Bank Index has recently broken out of its consolidation range and is moving higher.

With improving sectoral momentum and strong technical signals, Canara Bank appears well-positioned to lead the next leg of the PSU banking rally. Hence, accumulation is recommended in the Rs 130–134 zone, with a stop-loss at Rs 129. On the upside, the stock is likely to test Rs 139 in the short term.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 139
Stop-Loss: Rs 129
Multi Commodity Exchange of India | CMP: Rs 3,617.6

MCX India has registered a decisive breakout above its prolonged consolidation range of Rs 2,986–3,481, within which it had been trading since August 20. The breakout has been followed by strong upward momentum, with the stock scaling a fresh all-time high on November 11, indicating robust buying interest.
The ADX has started moving higher, signalling an emerging phase of strengthening trend momentum, while the MACD continues to gain traction, supported by rising green histogram bars.

Adding to the positive setup, the Capital Markets Index has also scaled a fresh all-time high. With strong sectoral tailwinds, MCX appears well-positioned to lead the next leg of the rally. Hence, accumulation is recommended in the Rs 3,605–3,625 zone, with a stop-loss at Rs 3,515. On the upside, the stock is likely to test Rs 3,860 in the short term.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 3,860
Stop-Loss: Rs 3,515
Vatsal Bhuva, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities
Punjab National Bank | CMP: Rs 138.48

PNB has witnessed a strong breakout above the falling neckline of a Cup and Handle pattern on the weekly chart, indicating the possibility of a fresh leg of bullish momentum. Additionally, the stock is sustaining comfortably above its key short-term and long-term moving averages, including the 20-day, 50-day and 200-day DMAs, reflecting strong positive sentiment.

However, the RSI is currently in a mildly overbought zone, so some consolidation cannot be ruled out. Hence, the stock can be considered for accumulation in the Rs 132–140 range, with a strict stop-loss at Rs 128 and an upside pattern target of Rs 160.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 155, Rs 160
Stop-Loss: Rs 128
Samvardhana Motherson International | CMP: Rs 169.69

Samvardhana Motherson International has witnessed a breakout from a falling channel on the daily chart, indicating a potential improvement in its overall technical structure. Notably, the lower boundary of the falling channel has consistently acted as a strong support during the corrective phase.

Additionally, the stock is now sustaining above all its crucial short-term, medium-term and long-term moving averages, namely the 20-day, 50-day, 100-day and 200-day DMAs, reflecting improving price strength. The RSI has also registered a bullish crossover, indicating a further improvement in momentum over the short term. Hence, the stock can be considered for accumulation in the Rs 165–168 range.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 180
Stop-Loss: Rs 161

title: Trade Spotlight: How should you trade Devyani International, FACT, Federal Bank, MCX India, Samvardhana Motherson, and others on November 12?
